title: Removal of calluses and corns (medical pedicure)
what: A specialist carefully removes hardened skin and calluses on your feet. It helps when walking hurts.
why: For calluses, corns with a core, cracked heels, and, with diabetes, for gentle foot care.
tell_doctor: If you have diabetes or poor circulation in your legs
If feeling in your feet is reduced
If you have a fungus, sores, or an ingrown nail

prepare.title: Feet
prepare.text: Do not soak your feet or cut calluses yourself before the procedure.

prepare.title: Shoes
prepare.text: Bring the shoes you wear most often, so the specialist can see what rubs.

prepare.title: Diabetes
prepare.text: With diabetes, do not cut calluses at home with blades, only with a specialist.

steps: The specialist examines your feet and nails
The skin is treated with an antiseptic
A product is applied to soften the hardened skin
Calluses and corns are removed with a device or an instrument
Your feet are treated and cream is applied
The specialist advises how to take pressure off your foot
feel: Usually painless, with some warmth or vibration
Removing a callus with a core can be unpleasant
after: Soft pads and insoles reduce pressure
Calluses return if the cause remains, so repeat the care
red_flags: Redness, swelling, pain, and pus where the callus was: see a doctor
With diabetes, any foot sore that does not heal: see a doctor right away

faq.q: Why does a callus come back?
faq.a: It is caused by pressure from shoes or the shape of your foot. The cause has to be removed with insoles and shoes.

faq.q: Can I have a pedicure with diabetes?
faq.a: Yes, a medical one with a specialist. Do not cut hard with blades or a pumice stone yourself.

reminders.text: Medical pedicure tomorrow. Do not cut anything at home, and bring your everyday shoes.
